chunk_findings.detail: `path_snapshot` drops every path whose entry is absent from `GE.worktree_entries`. If a post-round change is a deletion, the deleted path is absent from the worktree and, when it was not in `recorded`, it is also absent from `now`. `snapshot_differing` then takes `recorded.keys() | now.keys()`, which never contains that deleted path, so no difference is reported. Concrete input: `recorded={"a.py": "100644 abc"}` and `now_changed=["b.py"]`, where `b.py` was tracked but deleted after the review. Assuming `a.py` is unchanged, `snapshot_differing` returns `[]`; the guard lets an unreviewed deletion pass, violating the stated fail-closed behavior and the requirement that any edit to a changed/reviewed file after the round must block.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/reviewed_paths.py:24

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback test only asserts that the final gate outcome is `"failed"`. It creates two untracked files: `repo/other.txt` in the primary repo and `wt/notes.md` in the item worktree. If the whole-tree fallback were buggy and scanned the primary repo instead of the item worktree, it would still see `repo/other.txt` and return `"failed"`, so this assertion would pass. The test therefore does not verify that the fallback compares the correct tree; it should assert that the failure names `notes.md` and/or excludes `other.txt`.

chunk_findings.detail: A review round recorded by the pre-change `path_snapshot` is misread by the new `""` sentinel. Under the old writer, a reviewed path that was absent at review time (a deletion under review) was omitted from the recorded dict: `recorded = {"a.py": "100644 abc"}` while `gone.py` is reviewed and deleted, so it is absent from `recorded`. After this change, the same still-deleted `gone.py` is now included in `now` as `"gone.py": ""`. `snapshot_differing` unions the keys, sees `recorded.get("gone.py") is None` vs `now["gone.py"] == ""`, reports a difference, and blocks an already-reviewed deletion that did not change after the round. The change should version the snapshot field or, when consuming records written by the old format, treat a missing recorded key for an absent path as equal to the new `""` state.
